To determine $\mathrm{ex}_L(n, P_5)$ for $11 \mid n$, we consider the maximum size of a linear 3-graph containing no linear path of length 5 ($P_5$).

A linear path $P_k$ in a 3-uniform hypergraph has $2k+1$ vertices. For $k=5$, $P_5$ has $2(5)+1 = 11$ vertices and 5 edges. 

The extremal construction for avoiding $P_k$ in a linear 3-graph when $(2k+1) \mid n$ consists of disjoint copies of the maximum packing of triples (partial Steiner triple system) on $2k+1$ vertices:
- For $k = 3$, $2k+1 = 7$: the maximum packing of triples on 7 vertices is the Fano plane $PG(2, 2)$, which has 7 edges. It contains no $P_3$, giving $\mathrm{ex}_L(n, P_3) = \frac{7}{7}n = n$ when $7 \mid n$.
- For $k = 4$, $2k+1 = 9$: the maximum packing of triples on 9 vertices is the affine plane $AG(2, 3)$, which has 12 edges. It contains no $P_4$, giving $\mathrm{ex}_L(n, P_4) = \frac{12}{9}n = \frac{4}{3}n$ when $9 \mid n$.
- For $k = 5$, $2k+1 = 11$: the maximum packing of triples on 11 vertices achieves the Schönheim bound, which has $\left\lfloor \frac{11}{3} \left\lfloor \frac{10}{2} \right\rfloor \right\rfloor - 1 = 17$ edges (its leave is a 4-cycle $C_4$). This configuration contains no copy of $P_5$.

Taking $\frac{n}{11}$ disjoint copies of this 11-vertex configuration yields a $P_5$-free linear 3-graph on $n$ vertices with $\frac{17}{11}n$ edges, which achieves the maximum possible edge density.

ANSWER: \frac{17}{11}n
